header.scope: Lost: international traffic moved to Adyen's local acquiring and Stefan asked to split the contract; the US stayed with us, per the rep.
header.tag_why: Stefan judged us on approval rates by country, card type and issuer, and we answered with an average uplift while Adyen came back with a country-level test.

evidence.excerpt: A new head of payments. Stefan. They'd never had one.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Payments sat under an engineering manager, the guy who originally bought us, and he left last year.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: the first thing he did was pull declines by country
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I don't know exactly. He mentioned Brazil and a couple in Europe. I never saw his analysis.
evidence.label: fact

trigger.insight: This was not a product complaint. The account lost its owner when the buyer left, nobody on our side noticed for about a year, and the new owner's first move was to benchmark approvals. We don't know which markets looked bad or how bad, because the rep never saw the analysis that started this.
trigger.messaging: Write for the new payments leader in their first 90 days, whose first question is 'how are my approvals by country?', instead of for the developer who bought us.

evidence.excerpt: Stefan recommended it and the CFO approved.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: this went to the CFO two weeks ago.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: I can't take an average to my CFO.
evidence.label: quote

decider.insight: Stefan was the recommender and the CFO signed off, but we know that only from Stefan, and the rep never spoke to the CFO. By the time Stefan said it, the CFO had already approved, so we were arguing to someone who had stopped deciding. His line about the CFO shows the bar: a number specific to Kestrel.
decider.messaging: Give the payments owner a CFO-ready, customer-specific approvals case to carry upward, and stop assuming the champion can sell an average.

evidence.excerpt: Adyen ran a test on a slice of their international traffic and came back with results by country.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: local acquiring
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: I can't tell you what the test showed. He wouldn't share it.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: They got very specific. What's our approval rate in this country, on this card type, by issuer. And why.
evidence.label: fact

competitor.insight: Adyen won credibility by testing on Kestrel's real traffic and reporting by country. We don't know what the test showed, so we can't say whether local acquiring actually beat us or just looked more accountable. After meeting them, Stefan's questions moved from general to market, card type, issuer and reasons, which is a buyer comparing evidence.
competitor.messaging: Stop leading with the average-uplift claim (M4). Offer a live-traffic, market-by-market approvals comparison and prepare a direct answer on local acquiring in markets like Brazil and Europe.

evidence.excerpt: The Authorization Boost deck. The average uplift customers see.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: that's an average. What's mine?
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: Silence was the uplift number, like I said.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: He said it was the most useful thing we'd sent him.
evidence.label: fact

message.insight: The rep says 'we weren't really pitching', yet the generic deck was the answer and it was rejected outright. The only thing that got a positive reaction was the tailored analysis, and that was a paraphrase of what Stefan said. He also turned down the roadmap session, so he wanted evidence about his own numbers and had no interest in features.
message.messaging: Replace the average-uplift claim in M4 with an offer of a customer-specific approvals analysis, and treat renewals as a pitch with that analysis as the lead.

evidence.excerpt: I don't think there was a moment. It was kind of decided before we got in the room.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: this went to the CFO two weeks ago.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: that landed three weeks after he asked, and by then the test was finished.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Real findings. Things we could have fixed.
evidence.label: opinion

decided.insight: 'Nothing to do' doesn't hold up. Our own analysis found fixable problems, and it arrived three weeks after the request, after Adyen's test had finished. The rep also learned of the evaluation only at the renewal notice, after nine or ten months without a business review, so the loss was set up by slow response and no contact, not by a single moment.
decided.messaging: Make speed a claim: promise a market-by-market approvals diagnosis quickly, and back it with an internal commitment to deliver before a competitor test ends.

evidence.excerpt: A market-by-market view of their own approval rates, with reasons.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: that landed three weeks after he asked, and by then the test was finished.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: He asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month, and I didn't have a name.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I heard from Stripe when I said I was leaving.
evidence.label: quote

gaps.insight: We could produce the analysis, so the gap was timing and ownership more than capability. We had no named person watching his numbers, and Stefan felt we showed up only when he threatened to leave. The rep's 'healthy account, no tickets' read shows how little we were watching.
gaps.messaging: Extend M5 beyond response times: name an approvals owner who reviews each account's numbers on a regular cadence, and say so in the pitch.

evidence.excerpt: Money left on the table.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: Local cards, local rails.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: what's mine
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: He doesn't say "authorization," he says "approvals."
evidence.label: fact

language.insight: Stefan's words are plain and about money: approvals, money left on the table, what's mine. 'Local cards, local rails' sounds like the framing he took from Adyen, and our 'Authorization Boost' and 'Adaptive Acceptance' answer none of it.
language.messaging: Say 'approvals' instead of 'authorization' and write copy around 'your approval rate, by country, and the money you're leaving on the table'.

gaps.question: Which markets looked bad, and what did Stefan's declines analysis and Adyen's test show?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Elena whether Stefan would share the country list, and ask the payments performance team whether their analysis covered Brazil and the European markets and how they compared.

gaps.question: Was local acquiring actually the reason approvals were weak in those markets?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the payments performance team whether the fixable findings in the analysis involved local acquiring or something else.

gaps.question: How much volume moved, and what exactly did the split contract cover?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Elena for the post-split scope and volume by market, and confirm the US stayed from the customer, not just her read.

gaps.question: Who covered the account in the nine to ten months before the renewal, and why did the new head of payments go unnoticed?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the sales manager or account owner before Elena how coverage and the champion-departure alert worked.

gaps.question: What did the CFO need to see, and did anyone on our side speak to the CFO?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Elena whether she or anyone else had contact with the CFO or could ask Stefan what the CFO's criteria were.

close.rep_takeaway: A renewal is a pitch, and when the person who bought from you leaves, finding the new owner is urgent. When a buyer asks 'what's mine?', send their numbers fast, because an average and a three-week wait both read as a no.
